html:
Japan's main stock market, founded in Tokyo in 1878 under the Meiji government. It grew into one of the largest stock markets in the world.

It began trading in government bonds, many of them paid to former samurai when their stipends were ended, and then in shares of the new banks, railways and factories of modern Japan. The businessman Shibusawa Eiichi was among its founders. Osaka opened its own exchange the same year.

During the Second World War the exchanges were merged under state control, and trading stopped in 1945. The Tokyo Stock Exchange reopened in 1949 under new laws shaped by the American occupation.

Japan's postwar boom made it a giant. At the peak of the Japanese asset bubble around 1989, shares listed in Tokyo were worth more than those on the New York Stock Exchange. The crash that followed began decades of weak prices. Since 2013 the exchange has been part of Japan Exchange Group, along with Osaka.
sum: Japan's main stock market, founded in Tokyo in 1878 under the Meiji government. It grew into one of the largest stock markets in the world.
